cards.name: SL Blue Ice (Universal)
cards.summary: Icy cyan grade: cyan cast in shadows and mids, blues and skies pushed hard toward cyan, overall brightness kept; skin stays readable (saturation about 0.9x) but leans cool. Universal SpeedLooks version for ordinary Rec.709 video (phones, DSLRs in a standard profile, stock, news and web clips): the SpeedLooks 'Universal' camera-profile LUT feeds the look.
use_for: Cool, modern B-roll in AI / tech explainers
Background plates behind cold, data-heavy titles
avoid: Camera log footage (LogC, S-Log, C-Log, V-Log): the Universal patch expects ordinary video, so log stays flat with grey highlights (measured: 90% white lands near 0.6); use the matching camera variant, e.g. '(Arri Alexa)', or convert to Rec.709 first
Warm human stories and interviews: the cyan cast makes people look cold
Brand or party blues that must stay accurate: they turn cyan
cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color > Basic Correction > Input LUT = Lumetri/LUTs/Legacy/UNIVERSAL - SL - PROFILE.itx plus Creative > Look = Lumetri/Looks/Legacy/Blue Ice.look (LUT card 'Blue Ice'); Creative > Look 'SL BLUE ICE' as an unverified single-LUT substitute
cards.scripting: Premiere's scripting API cannot apply .prfpset presets by name. Parsed from Lumetri Presets.prfpset: one Lumetri Color (AE.ADBE Lumetri), saved by an older 98-parameter Lumetri, with only two non-default settings: Basic Correction > Input LUT = legacy value 32 and Creative > Look = legacy value 6 (Intensity 100). Both legacy lists are sorted by name (the Look list also holds the Cinespace, Fuji, Kodak and Monochrome looks), so Look 6 is Lumetri/Looks/Legacy/Blue Ice.look (one LUT layer; data in Lumetri/LUTs/Legacy/BLUE ICE - SL - 3527.itx), and Input LUT 32 is the last SpeedLooks camera profile after REDLOGFILM (29): Lumetri/LUTs/Legacy/UNIVERSAL - SL - PROFILE.itx, the generic 'Universal' camera patch (the camera variants use 8 = Arri Alexa to 29 = REDLOGFILM). That mapping is inferred from the sort order and the LUT maths (the patch compresses ordinary video into the log-like space the look expects), not checked in the UI. Do NOT copy 32 / 6 into pr_props: PR 2026 exposes 'Input LUT' 0-11 and 'Look' 0-68 over different, install-dependent lists that do not include these legacy files, and LUTAsset / LookAsset are strings a spec cannot set; whether PR 2026 still resolves the legacy values when the preset is dragged on by hand is untested, so check a rendered frame. Exact route: apply the preset by hand (or Input LUT > Browse to UNIVERSAL - SL - PROFILE.itx and Look > Browse to Blue Ice.look), then reuse it with copy / paste attributes; outside Premiere, chain the two .itx files (binary ITX3: 40-byte header, then 32x32x32 float32 RGB, red index fastest) into one .cube. To soften the grade, put it on an adjustment layer and lower that layer's Opacity: lowering Creative 'Intensity#2' alone leaves the Universal patch at full strength, so the picture goes flat and washed-out. Premiere-native single-LUT substitute: Creative > Look 'SL BLUE ICE' (Lumetri/LUTs/Creative/SL BLUE ICE.itx, encrypted, so its match to this preset is unverified); its Look index is probably 22 (None + Creative folder sorted by name), but the harvested menu has 69 entries (0-68), so read the live Look menu labels before using {"Look": 22, "Intensity#2": 100}. Rough scriptable stand-in for Rec.709 footage: the 'approx' Lumetri Color pr_props (cast, tone and saturation only, eyeballed from the measurements, not verified). Measured on the installed LUT data (Universal profile then look, trilinear, Rec.709 test values): grey 0.18/0.45/0.80 -> 0.16/0.47/0.86 (luma); mid grey 0.45 -> R/G/B 0.37/0.50/0.54; skin saturation x0.91 (mean of three skin tones).

Rough scriptable stand-in for Rec.709 footage: the 'approx' Lumetri Color pr_props (cast, tone and saturation only, eyeballed from the measurements, not verified). cards.name: Full to Legal Range, 10-bit
cards.summary: Technical range fix: one Lumetri Color whose Input LUT is FullToSMPTE10.cube, an extended-domain LUT that maps -0.073..1.095 (the 10-bit full-range codes read as legal range) onto 0..1. On a full-range clip that Premiere decoded as legal range it brings the crushed blacks and clipped whites back (only if the out-of-range values survived decoding); on correctly decoded footage it just squeezes 0..1 into 64/1023..940/1023, giving greyer blacks and dimmer whites. A fix, not a creative look.
use_for: Fix 10-bit ProRes / HEVC / camera files that look crushed and over-contrasty because full-range data is being read as legal range
OBS or screen recordings captured in full range but flagged (or read) as limited: crushed shadows and clipped highlights next to normal camera clips
avoid: On correctly decoded footage it only washes the image out: check the waveform first (blacks piled at 0 and whites flat at 100)
As a broadcast-safe / legaliser pass: Premiere already maps 0..1 to legal 16-235 when it encodes, so this squeezes twice (grey blacks, dim whites on air); use Video Limiter for that
Stacking it with a Legal to Full preset or a second range fix
Using the wrong bit-depth variant: pick the one matching the source (10-bit here); in float the 8 / 10 / 12-bit variants differ by under 0.3%
cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color > Basic Correction > Input LUT = Lumetri/LUTs/Legacy/FullToSMPTE10.cube (LUT card 'FullToSMPTE10'); Levels for a script-only version
cards.scripting: Premiere's scripting API cannot apply .prfpset presets by name. The preset (saved by an older 98-parameter Lumetri) sets only Basic Correction > Input LUT = custom (legacy value 1) with FullToSMPTE10.cube embedded in the Lumetri blob (the stored path is Adobe's build machine, ending Lumetri/LUTs/Legacy/FullToSMPTE10.cube; the installed copy is Lumetri/LUTs/Legacy/FullToSMPTE10.cube in the Premiere folder), with Look = None and every other control neutral. The legacy LUT is not in today's 'Input LUT' popup (0-11, install-dependent) and the 'LUTAsset' file blob cannot be set from a spec, so the exact Lumetri route is manual (apply the preset, or Input LUT > Browse). Script-only equivalent for the squeeze: {"name": "Levels", "pr_props": {"(RGB) Black Output Level": 16, "(RGB) White Output Level": 235}}. Levels works in 8-bit 0-255 units; 16/235 matches 10-bit 64/940 and 12-bit 256/3760 within about one 8-bit code. Unlike the extended-domain LUT, Levels probably clips values outside 0..1 before remapping (not verified), so it cannot recover the crushed shadow / clipped highlight detail of a misread full-range clip; use the LUT for that. Check the waveform before and after.
